affiliations.date_precision: Civilian-occupation value 992 was recorded at Army entry on 8 April 1943. NARA's corrected code table defines 9-92 as Students; no institution, course, employment, start date or later Army-to-OSS transfer date is identified.
affiliations.research_notes: The exact private identifier and exact name confirm the Army row. Student status is not employment, and no school is inferred from later biographies or namesakes.

affiliations.date_precision: Civilian-occupation value 732 was recorded at Army entry on 17 November 1941. NARA's code table defines 7-32 as Construction occupations, n.e.c.; no trade, employer, project, workplace, start date or Army-to-OSS sequence is identified.

affiliations.role_title: Psychotherapist and psychiatry department faculty member
affiliations.date_precision: A scholarly history dates Dai's Duke psychiatry appointment to 1943. The OSS staff volume labels Duke as his official institution before government service and lists work at Fairfax and Kunming; the exact government-enrollment date and leave arrangement are not stated.
affiliations.research_notes: The direct OSS source defines parenthetical institutions as preceding government service. Institutional and scholarly sources establish that Dai held a teaching and psychiatry appointment rather than merely attending Duke.

affiliations.role_title: Teacher and assistant professor in medical psychology
affiliations.date_precision: Appalachian State dates the faculty appointment to 1935 and departure to 1939. The scholarly article says Dai taught medical psychology from 1935 and served as assistant professor from 1936 until leaving China in 1939.
affiliations.research_notes: This is earlier documented pre-OSS employment. Duke, not Peking Union Medical College, is the direct OSS source's named institution immediately before government service.
